 White was initially listed as probable for Tuesday’s game, so the status upgrade was expected. He’ll fill his usual spot in the Celtics’ starting lineup.

 Derrick White amassed 24 points (7-of-18 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks. 
 White has gotten off to a slow start, as he began Wednesday averaging 11.1 points per game. With Jayson Tatum out, the Celtics guard had more room to attack offensively, and he took advantage. White shot 1-of-7 from beyond the arc, which hurt his overall field-goal percentage, but he finished with a season-high point total and a complete stat line. The “buy low” window may have closed with this performance. 
 Derrick White 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Derrick White tallied 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Magic. 
 White took a back seat offensively on Sunday, but he did a little bit of everything to help the Celtics end their week with a victory. After shooting a career-worst 39.4 percent from the field last season, White is up to 47.4 percent through six games. His category-league value hasn’t reached his ADP yet, but fantasy managers shouldn’t worry. 
 Derrick White 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Derrick White tallied 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, four steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Hornets. 
 White is coming off his worst season in field-goal percentage, making just 39.4 percent of his attempts. However, he still provided top-50 fantasy value because of everything else he does to help the Celtics win. Fantasy managers should expect White to bounce back with his shooting while still offering reliable fantasy value across the board. His ceiling may be somewhat limited, but his fantasy floor is strong and reliable. 
 Derrick White 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Derrick White amassed 26 points (9-of-26 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three blocks and five three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 7 loss to the 76ers. 
 White got his Game 7 off to an excellent start, scoring 19 points in the first half. However, the 76ers, specifically VJ Edgecombe, did a much better job of defending him in the second half. White made some history, joining Kevin Durant (2018) and Robert Covington (2020) as the only players to record at least five three-pointers and three blocks in a Game 7, but it wasn’t enough to get the shorthanded Celtics over the finish line. Shooting was an issue for the Celtics’ guard throughout the season, but the ability to fill a stat line preserved his fantasy value. Managers should expect more of the same from White in 2026-27, hopefully with a more accurate jump shot. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard tallied 32 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and six three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 4 win over the 76ers. 
 On a day when starter Derrick White (6/6/3/1/2 with two three-pointers) attempted just five shots, Pritchard stepped up with one of the best outings of his postseason career. The 32 points, a playoff career-high for Pritchard, were two shy of the Celtics franchise record for most in a playoff game by a reserve, which Kevin McHale still holds. While he made too many starts to qualify for NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors, Pritchard remains one of the best reserve scorers in the league. And he reminded Philadelphia of that in Game 4. The Celtics will look to close out the series on Tuesday night.

 Guard 
 #9 
 Derrick White tallied 10 points (4-of-10 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 1 win over the 76ers. 
 With six players in double figures and stars Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum combining to score 51 points, the Celtics did not need much scoring from White. Shooting 2-of-7 from three, the veteran guard dished out six assists and committed just one turnover. White’s ability to fill the stat line is what made him so valuable to fantasy managers during the regular season, and it has made him an important piece in Boston since his acquisition during the 2021-22 campaign.

 Derrick White (knee) and Neemias Queta (toe) are out for Sunday’s game against the Magic. 
 The Celtics have already ruled out four of their five starters for Sunday’s regular-season finale, as the outcome will not impact their playoff seeding. White’s absence should free up additional minutes for Ron Harper Jr. and Max Shulga. As for Queta, there will be more playing time available for Luka Garza, and Amari Williams could get rotation minutes as well.

 Derrick White (knee) is available for Friday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 White will play both games of the Celtics’ back-to-back, with the team still one win away from guaranteeing itself the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs. The Pelicans are shorthanded, so this may be a spot where the Celtics can give their available regulars a little more time on the bench.

 Derrick White (knee) is available to play against the Knicks on Thursday. 
 Despite dealing with a knee contusion, White will be available on Thursday when the Celtics take the floor at Madison Square Garden. White provides high-level perimeter defense and a balance of scoring and playmaking on the offensive end. He’s averaged 18.7 points against the Knicks in their three matchups this season.

 Derrick White (knee) was present at shootaround ahead of Thursday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Questionable with a right knee contusion, White did some shooting during Thursday’s pregame session and was in his practice uniform. However, Jaylen Brown (Achilles) was not in uniform. Both remain questionable for Thursday night’s game, with the Celtics one win away from sewing up the No. 2 seed in the East.

 Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
 The Mavericks had no answer for Victor Wembanyama and looked set to get blown out. However, Marshall got going in the second half, shooting 7-of-9 from the field and scoring 17 points. Marshall remains a player who can be rostered in deep leagues, even though he’ll come off the bench on most nights.

 Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.
 After shooting 3-of-19 from the field in Monday’s loss to the Kings, Flagg got off to a terribly slow start on Wednesday. The reigning Rookie of the Year missed all seven of his shots in the first quarter and started 1-of-11 from the field. The good news is that Flagg shot 6-of-8 the rest of the way. Add in the rebounds and assists, and the final stat line was solid, but category managers would have wanted to see more defensive stats. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Luka’s MVP campaign continues in Sacramento where he puts another massive statement game against the Kings.  Dylan Harper finished Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks with 21 points (9-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds and one three-pointer.
 Having entered the season with an ADP of 80, Harper has exceeded that number by a safe distance thus far. While his final line against the Spurs did not include any assists, steals or blocks, the second-year guard was efficient enough to still offer solid fantasy value. With it unknown when Tobias Harris (calf) will be available, Harper should not struggle to maintain his current production.

 Austin Reaves put up 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, and a three in win over the Kings.
 Austin has been one of the most consistent players in the league this season. He does his job as the secondary option in the offense, he hits threes, he gets some assists and plays good defense. The rebounds have been lower than what you would want since he’s been averaging 4 rebounds a game for the past three seasons, and he’s at three this year, but it’s hard to complain all things considered.
